task: feat(runtime): pass host devices from STRIX_DOCKER_SANDBOX_DEVICES through to the sandbox container
description:
## Summary

The docker runtime never passed host devices to the sandbox container, so anything that needs a device node inside the sandbox could not run: a tunnel brought up in the sandbox (OpenVPN, WireGuard, Tailscale) needs `/dev/net/tun`, and Docker's default device cgroup denies it even though the container already has `NET_ADMIN`/`NET_RAW`.

`docker_client.py` gains `STRIX_DOCKER_SANDBOX_DEVICES`, a comma-separated list of host device paths; each is mapped to the same path in the container with `rwm` access at create time, next to the existing network and resource-limit handling:

```
STRIX_DOCKER_SANDBOX_DEVICES=/dev/net/tun  ->  devices=["/dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun:rwm"]
```

Unset means no extra devices, so the default sandbox is unchanged. Entries already present in `create_kwargs["devices"]` are kept and not duplicated.

Tests in `tests/test_docker_client_devices.py`: unset env adds nothing; two devices map to same-path `rwm` specs; an existing device list is kept without duplicates.

Part of STR-1669

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/54414ea3ecb34ade9189534e5c690969
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/54414ea3ecb34ade9189534e5c690969?variant=devin

diff --git a/strix/runtime/docker_client.py b/strix/runtime/docker_client.py
index 969267d53..68ffa2fba 100644
--- a/strix/runtime/docker_client.py
+++ b/strix/runtime/docker_client.py
@@ -66,6 +66,33 @@ def _apply_sandbox_network(create_kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
         create_kwargs.pop("ports", None)
 
 
+_SANDBOX_DEVICES_ENV = "STRIX_DOCKER_SANDBOX_DEVICES"
+
+
+def _sandbox_devices() -> list[str]:
+    raw = os.environ.get(_SANDBOX_DEVICES_ENV, "")
+    return [item.strip() for item in raw.split(",") if item.strip()]
+
+
+def _apply_sandbox_devices(create_kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Pass the host devices listed in ``STRIX_DOCKER_SANDBOX_DEVICES`` through.
+
+    Comma-separated device paths, each mapped to the same path in the container
+    with ``rwm`` access. A tunnel brought up inside the sandbox (OpenVPN,
+    Tailscale) needs ``/dev/net/tun``: Docker's default device cgroup denies it
+    even with ``NET_ADMIN``. Unset means no extra devices.
+    """
+    devices = _sandbox_devices()
+    if not devices:
+        return
+    existing = [str(item) for item in (create_kwargs.get("devices") or [])]
+    for path in devices:
+        spec = f"{path}:{path}:rwm"
+        if spec not in existing and path not in existing:
+            existing.append(spec)
+    create_kwargs["devices"] = existing
+
+
 def _apply_resource_limits(create_kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
     """Apply optional cgroup resource caps from the environment. Unset/blank
     values leave docker's default (unbounded), so this is opt-in per host."""
@@ -233,6 +260,7 @@ async def _create_container(
         extra_hosts["host.docker.internal"] = "host-gateway"
 
         _apply_sandbox_network(create_kwargs)
+        _apply_sandbox_devices(create_kwargs)
         _apply_resource_limits(create_kwargs)
         _apply_log_limits(create_kwargs)
         _apply_run_labels(create_kwargs)

+"""``STRIX_DOCKER_SANDBOX_DEVICES`` passes host devices through to the sandbox container."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from strix.runtime import docker_client
+
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    import pytest
+
+
+def test_unset_adds_no_devices(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.delenv(docker_client._SANDBOX_DEVICES_ENV, raising=False)
+    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {}
+    docker_client._apply_sandbox_devices(kwargs)
+    assert kwargs == {}
+
+
+def test_devices_are_mapped_to_the_same_path_rwm(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setenv(docker_client._SANDBOX_DEVICES_ENV, " /dev/net/tun, /dev/kvm ,,")
+    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {}
+    docker_client._apply_sandbox_devices(kwargs)
+    assert kwargs["devices"] == ["/dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun:rwm", "/dev/kvm:/dev/kvm:rwm"]
+
+
+def test_existing_devices_are_kept_and_not_duplicated(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setenv(docker_client._SANDBOX_DEVICES_ENV, "/dev/fuse,/dev/net/tun")
+    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {"devices": ["/dev/fuse"]}
+    docker_client._apply_sandbox_devices(kwargs)
+    assert kwargs["devices"] == ["/dev/fuse", "/dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun:rwm"]

task: feat(guardrails): add native Reco guardrail provider (pre_call), fail closed by default
description:
Carries https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/38527 by @RecoLabs-YaronBratspiess and @MickeyShnaiderman-RecoLabs to completion. Adds Reco as a native pre-call guardrail on top of `GenericGuardrailAPI`, rebased onto main, with one change on top of their work: the guardrail now fails closed by default like every other guardrail here. We could not push to the fork branch, so this PR supersedes #38527 with their commits kept as authors

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Reco had no native guardrail, admins hand-rolled the generic guardrail API config
- Header names and tenant ids were only validated when a request reached Reco
- The original PR let traffic through uninspected on any Reco error by default

How it solves it:

- `guardrail: reco` registers a first-class provider built on `GenericGuardrailAPI`
- `reco_tenant_id` is UUID-validated at startup and sent as `X-Reco-Tenant-Id`
- BLOCKED responses raise with the configured guardrail name, not the generic one
- `fail_on_error` defaults to `true` and `unreachable_fallback` to `fail_closed`

Intentional product change: a Reco outage or error now blocks the request unless the admin sets `fail_on_error: false`. The original PR defaulted to fail-open

## User Flow

Before: an admin who wants Reco has no provider to pick

1. The admin sets `guardrail: reco` in config.yaml
2. The proxy logs `Skipping guardrail 'reco-guardrail' ... Unsupported guardrail: reco` and serves traffic with no guardrail at all

After: Reco is a supported guardrail with safe defaults

1. The admin sets `guardrail: reco` with `reco_tenant_id` and `api_base` under `optional_params`
2. The proxy starts, and a malformed tenant id fails at startup instead of at request time
3. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt Reco's policy blocks and gets 400 `Blocked by Reco policy: ...`
4. A permitted prompt reaches the real model and returns 200
5. If Reco is unreachable the request is blocked with 500 `Generic Guardrail API failed`, unless `fail_on_error: false` is set

## Relevant issues

Supersedes #38527

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Proxy from source on port 4012 with a real Anthropic key. We have no Reco tenant, so `RECO_API_BASE` points at a local stand-in that speaks the Generic Guardrail API wire format (`POST /beta/litellm_basic_guardrail_api`, answers `BLOCKED` when the text contains "hateful", `NONE` otherwise, and logs the `X-Reco-Tenant-Id` header it received). The permitted request goes to the live model. The contributors' original run against a live Reco preprod tenant is in #38527

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: reco-guardrail
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: reco
      mode: pre_call
      default_on: true
      optional_params:
        reco_tenant_id: os.environ/RECO_TENANT_ID
        api_base: os.environ/RECO_API_BASE
```

### Before (560372456e)

1. `litellm --config config.yaml` with the config above
2. The proxy starts without the guardrail and logs `Skipping guardrail 'reco-guardrail': invalid configuration, proxy is starting WITHOUT this guardrail: Unsupported guardrail: reco`, so every request goes to the model uninspected

### After (8e9cf67da1)

#### Blocked request

1. `curl -s -w ' http=%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:4012/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-proof-reco' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"model":"claude-ha

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..a15a372c462e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/reco/__init__.py
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from types import MappingProxyType
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, TypeAdapter
+
+from litellm.secret_managers.main import get_secret_str
+from litellm.types.guardrails import SupportedGuardrailIntegrations
+from litellm.types.proxy.guardrails.guardrail_hooks.reco import RecoOptionalParams
+
+from .reco import RecoGuardrail
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from litellm.types.guardrails import Guardrail, LitellmParams
+
+_CONFIG_MAPPING: Final = TypeAdapter(Mapping[str, object])
+
+
+def _optional_params_mapping(optional_params: object) -> Mapping[str, object]:
+    """optional_params arrives as a pydantic object from YAML, or as a plain dict when reconciled from the DB."""
+    if optional_params is None:
+        return MappingProxyType({})
+    raw: Final = (
+        optional_params.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) if isinstance(optional_params, BaseModel) else optional_params
+    )
+    return _CONFIG_MAPPING.validate_python(raw)
+
+
+def _first_configured(field_name: str, sources: tuple[Mapping[str, object], ...]) -> object:
+    value: Final = next((source[field_name] for source in sources if source.get(field_name) is not None), None)
+    if isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("os.environ/"):
+        return get_secret_str(value)
+    return value
+
+
+def initialize_guardrail(litellm_params: "LitellmParams", guardrail: "Guardrail") -> RecoGuardrail:
+    import litellm
+
+    # Top-level fields only count when set explicitly: their defaults are fail-closed and would flip Reco's.
+    explicit_top_level: Final = _CONFIG_MAPPING.validate_python(
+        litellm_params.model_dump(include=litellm_params.model_fields_set & RecoOptionalParams.model_fields.keys())
+    )
+    sources: Final = (_optional_params_mapping(litellm_params.optional_params), explicit_top_level)
+    configured: Final = (
+        (field_name, _first_configured(field_name, sources)) for field_name in RecoOptionalParams.model_fields
+    )
+    reco_params: Final = RecoOptionalParams.model_validate(
+        {field_name: value for field_name, value in configured if value is not None}
+    )
+
+    _reco_callback: Final = RecoGuardrail(
+        guardrail_name=guardrail["guardrail_name"],
+        reco_tenant_id=reco_params.reco_tenant_id,
+        api_base=reco_params.api_base,
+        unreachable_fallback=reco_params.unreachable_fallback,
+        fail_on_error=reco_params.fail_on_error,
+        event_hook=litellm_params.mode,
+        default_on=bool(litellm_params.default_on),
+    )
+    litellm.logging_callback_manager.add_litellm_callback(_reco_callback)
+
+    return _reco_callback
+
+
+guardrail_initializer_registry: Final = {
+    SupportedGuardrailIntegrations.RECO.value: initialize_guardrail,
+}
+
+
+guardrail_class_registry: Final = {
+    SupportedGuardrailIntegrations.RECO.value: RecoGuardrail,
+}
diff --git a/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/reco/reco.py b/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/reco/reco.py

--- /dev/null
+++ b/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/reco/reco.py
@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Final, Literal, Optional
+
+from litellm.exceptions import GuardrailRaisedException
+from litellm.integrations.custom_guardrail import (
+    log_guardrail_information,  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType]  # decorator is untyped
+)
+from litellm.proxy.guardrails.guardrail_hooks.generic_guardrail_api.generic_guardrail_api import (
+    GenericGuardrailAPI,
+)
+from litellm.types.guardrails import GuardrailEventHooks, Mode
+from litellm.types.proxy.guardrails.guardrail_hooks.reco import validate_reco_tenant_id
+from litellm.types.utils import GenericGuardrailAPIInputs
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from litellm.litellm_core_utils.litellm_logging import Logging as LiteLLMLoggingObj
+    from litellm.types.proxy.guardrails.guardrail_hooks.base import GuardrailConfigModel
+    from litellm.types.proxy.guardrails.guardrail_hooks.reco import RecoOptionalParams
+
+
+class RecoGuardrail(GenericGuardrailAPI):
+    """Reco guardrail integration for LiteLLM, built on the Generic Guardrail API wire contract."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        reco_tenant_id: str | None,
+        api_base: str | None,
+        headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
+        unreachable_fallback: Literal["fail_closed", "fail_open"] = "fail_closed",
+        fail_on_error: bool = True,
+        guardrail_name: str | None = None,
+        event_hook: str | Sequence[str] | Mode | None = None,
+        default_on: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        if not reco_tenant_id:
+            raise ValueError("reco_tenant_id is required for the Reco guardrail")
+        if not api_base:
+            raise ValueError("api_base is required for the Reco guardrail")
+
+        validated_tenant_id: Final = validate_reco_tenant_id(reco_tenant_id)
+
+        super().__init__(  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # parent takes untyped extra_headers and **kwargs
+            headers={**(headers or {}), "X-Reco-Tenant-Id": validated_tenant_id},
+            api_base=api_base,
+            unreachable_fallback=unreachable_fallback,
+            fail_on_error=fail_on_error,
+            guardrail_name=guardrail_name,
+            event_hook=event_hook,
+            default_on=default_on,
+        )
+
+    @log_guardrail_information
+    async def apply_guardrail(
+        self,
+        inputs: GenericGuardrailAPIInputs,
+        request_data: dict[str, object],  # mutable-ok: must match GenericGuardrailAPI.apply_guardrail's own param type
+        input_type: Literal["request", "response"],
+        logging_obj: Optional["LiteLLMLoggingObj"] = None,
+    ) -> GenericGuardrailAPIInputs:
+        # GenericGuardrailAPI raises with a hardcoded module-level guardrail_name on BLOCKED,
+        # not the guardrail's own configured name. Re-raise with the right one instead of
+        # patching the shared base class.
+        try:
+            return await super().apply_guardrail(  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # parent annotates request_data as a bare dict
+                inputs=inputs, request_data=request_data, input_type=input_type, logging_obj=logging_obj
+            )
+        except GuardrailRaisedException as e:
+            raise GuardrailRaisedException(
+                guardrail_name=self.guardrail_name,
+                message=e.message,
+                should_wrap_with_default_message=False,
+                status_code=e.status_code,
+                blocked_content=e.blocked_content,
+            ) from e
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def get_config_model() -> type["GuardrailConfigModel[RecoOptionalParams]"] | None:
+        from litellm.types.proxy.guardrails.guardrail_hooks.reco import RecoConfigModel
+
+        return RecoConfigModel
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_supported_event_hooks(cls) -> list[GuardrailEventHooks]:  # mutable-ok: fixed by base class
+        return [GuardrailEventHooks.pre_call]

+import uuid
+from typing import Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator
+
+from .base import GuardrailConfigModel
+
+
+def validate_reco_tenant_id(value: str) -> str:
+    try:
+        uuid.UUID(value)
+    except ValueError as e:
+        raise ValueError(f"reco_tenant_id must be a valid UUID, got {value!r}") from e
+    return value
+
+
+class RecoOptionalParams(BaseModel):
+    """Configuration parameters for the Reco guardrail"""
+
+    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
+
+    reco_tenant_id: str = Field(
+        description="Tenant identifier for the Reco account, as a UUID. Sent as the X-Reco-Tenant-Id header on every guardrail request.",
+    )
+    api_base: str = Field(
+        description="Base URL for the Reco guardrail API. Reco's endpoint is per-region and per-silo, so this must be set explicitly rather than defaulted.",
+    )
+    unreachable_fallback: Literal["fail_closed", "fail_open"] = Field(
+        default="fail_closed",
+        description="Behavior when Reco is unreachable. 'fail_closed' (default) blocks the request; 'fail_open' lets it through uninspected. Only applies while fail_on_error is true.",
+    )
+    fail_on_error: bool = Field(
+        default=True,
+        description="Behavior on any Reco error, including unreachability. True (default) blocks the request; False lets it through uninspected.",
+    )
+
+    @field_validator("reco_tenant_id")
+    @classmethod
+    def _check_reco_tenant_id(cls, v: str) -> str:
+        return validate_reco_tenant_id(v)
+
+
+class RecoConfigModel(GuardrailConfigModel[RecoOptionalParams]):
+    """Configuration parameters for the Reco guardrail"""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def ui_friendly_name() -> str:
+        return "Reco"

task: fix(router): skip declared text-only deployments for image requests on every routing strategy
description:
Image requests in a model group that mixes vision and text-only deployments no longer land on a text-only deployment. The router already knew how to skip deployments declared `supports_vision: false`, but only when `enable_pre_call_checks: true` was set, which almost nobody sets, so a latency-routed group with an OpenAI vision model and a Bedrock gpt-oss model kept sending images to gpt-oss and returning its 400. The skip now runs on every routing strategy by default, and chat completion errors now carry `x-litellm-model-id` so you can tell which deployment failed.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Vision filter from #48152 only ran under `enable_pre_call_checks: true`
- Default config still sent image requests to text-only deployments
- Chat 400s had no `x-litellm-model-id`, so the failing deployment was unknown

How it solves it:

- Filter moved out of `_pre_call_checks` and runs on every request, right after the pre-call block and before order filtering and strategy selection
- Same rules: skip only explicit or cost-map `supports_vision: false`, unknown stays eligible
- All text-only group keeps every deployment so the provider error still surfaces
- `maybe_get_model_id` also reads the chat request metadata the router fills in

## User Flow

Before: a user sending an image to a mixed `mixed` group gets a Bedrock 400 on most tries

1. Admin runs `mixed` with `openai/gpt-5.6` and `bedrock/openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0` under `latency-based-routing`, nothing else set
2. User sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with an `image_url` part
3. Response is `400 This model doesn't support the image content block` with no `x-litellm-model-id` header
4. Retrying sometimes returns 200 from the OpenAI deployment, so the user sees it as flaky

After: the same request always reaches the vision deployment

1. Admin runs the same config
2. User sends the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with an `image_url` part
3. Response is 200 every time and `x-litellm-model-id` names the OpenAI deployment, the same on POST /v1/responses with `input_image`
4. A plain text request still lands on either deployment

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-9792

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy, real OpenAI and Bedrock calls, no mocks. Config used for both runs:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mixed
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.6
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
    model_info:
      id: oai-vision
  - model_name: mixed
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
    model_info:
      id: bedrock-gpt-oss

router_settings:
  routing_strategy: latency-based-routing
```

Each case loops the same curl and prints the status line, the `x-litellm-model-id` header and the first line of the body:

```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do
  curl -s -D - -o body.json localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"mixed","messages":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"What color is this image? One word."},{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"'"$IMG"'"}}]}]}' \
    | grep -i "^HTTP\|x-litellm-model-id"; head -c 110 body.json
done

Carries https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/47853 by @hardawaykwork to completion. Retrieve, update and delete on an Azure OpenAI vector store returned 404 because the store id was appended after the `?api-version=` query string. <summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Azure vector store retrieve, update and delete sent `vector_stores?api-version=...%2F<id>`
- Azure answered 404 Resource not found for every one of them
- #41384 only fixed `/search`, which builds its own URL

task: fix(router): keep latency routing alive when latency samples are unusable
description:
Carries https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/47325 by @Bytechoreographer to completion. One negative or NaN first-token latency sample made latency-based routing return 500 for the whole model group until the cache entry expired. This keeps his fix commit as is, rebased onto main, and updates one test for the `latency_normalized` key main now reads. We could not push to the fork branch, so this PR supersedes #47325 with authorship kept

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- One negative or NaN latency sample empties the routing window for a model group
- Every request to that group then returns 500 until the cache entry expires
- Successful calls have recorded TTFT near -600s when the two timestamps invert

How it solves it:

- Non-finite and negative samples are dropped before deployments are ranked
- An empty window falls back to every candidate instead of raising IndexError
- Poisoned cache entries heal on deploy, no Redis flush needed
- The fallback test now seeds `latency_normalized`, which main reads since #47727
- The new tests assert `_latency_per_deployment`, so unfiltered samples fail deterministically

## User Flow

Before: a developer streaming to a latency-routed model group gets a 500 after one bad sample lands in the routing cache

1. The proxy admin configures `routing_strategy: latency-based-routing` with `lowest_latency_buffer: 5`
2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true`
3. An earlier successful call recorded a TTFT of -602 seconds, so the group's cached samples now average negative
4. The same POST returns 500 with `{"error":{"type":"api_error","message":"Cannot choose from an empty sequence"}}`
5. It keeps returning 500 until the routing cache entry expires, one hour by default

After: the same request streams a normal answer

1. The proxy admin keeps the same routing settings
2. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true`
3. The negative sample is ignored when the group is ranked
4. The same POST returns 200 and streams the model's answer

## Affected release

Regression since v1.102.0. `be9a2ea7c97` made `_average_latency` average every sample instead of ignoring non-float ones, and `699ae63b2a3` (#40352) started storing raw TTFT seconds for every streaming request. A cache entry holding one negative or NaN sample now produces a negative average, and `lowest_latency_buffer` pushes the lower bound below every candidate

- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally

Live before/after from #47325, captured by the author at `748c973f42` (base) and `5e227af82a` (his fix commit, byte-identical to the one carried here). Setup: a proxy running from source with one model pointed at a live upstream, `routing_strategy: latency-based-routing`, `lowest_latency_buffer: 5`, Redis on 127.0.0.1:6390. One real streaming call writes `haiku_map`, then the entry is set to `"time_to_first_token_seconds": [-602.0]`, which is the shape production reaches on its own when `completion_start_time` lands before `start_time`. task: fix(ci): write the tools coverage profile under build/gocoverdir, not over the tools shard's
description:
## What and why

develop's first CircleCI pipeline on the ten-shard split (4771) went red on the coverage job's `tools` node after every package had passed:

```
tail: error writing 'standard output': No space left on device
make[1]: *** [Makefile:371: coverage] Error 1
```

The cause is a filename collision, not disk pressure. `make coverage-shard SHARD=tools` collects into `COVERAGE_PROFILE=coverage-tools.txt`, and `make coverage` wrote the tools module's own `-coverpkg` profile to `../coverage-tools.txt` — the same file — and then ran `tail -n +2 coverage-tools.txt >> coverage-tools.txt`, appending the file to itself without end until the disk was full. It is deterministic: pipeline 4773 failed the same node at the same step after 21 minutes. Before the split the tools module's coverage ran on the `runtime` node, whose profile is `coverage-runtime.txt`, so the two names never met.

The tools profile now lives under `GO_COUNTER_DIR` (`build/gocoverdir/tools.txt`), with the other intermediate counters of the run: the directory is cleared at the start of every `make coverage`, and no shard's `coverage-<shard>.txt` can be in it, so no shard name can collide with it again. The `rm` of the intermediate goes with the move.

## How it was verified

- `tests/hygiene/coverage_profiles_test.go` (new, `TestCoverageIntermediatesCannotBeAShardProfile`): parses the Makefile's `coverage` recipe for every profile it writes besides `$(COVERAGE_PROFILE)` (`-coverprofile=`, `-o`, the `tail -n +2 … >>` sources) and fails if one is outside `$(GO_COUNTER_DIR)/` or is named `coverage-<shard>.txt` for any shard of the CircleCI coverage array or the Makefile's `COVERAGE_SHARDS` (or `coverage.txt`). On develop's Makefile it fails three ways (`../coverage-tools.txt` outside GO_COUNTER_DIR and named like the tools shard's profile); on this branch it passes.
- Reproduced locally on `origin/develop` with `make coverage-shard SHARD=tools`: the `tests/wasm` step is harmless (9.5 MB profile, empty `gocoverdir`), then the tools step's `tail` grew `coverage-tools.txt` without bound (killed at 4 GB of growth).
- Full `make coverage-shard SHARD=tools` on this branch: exit 0 in 339 s, all 29 tools packages `ok` plus `tests/wasm`; `df` used before 66.97 GB, after 67.39 GB (+0.42 GB, build cache included); `build/gocoverdir/tools.txt` 142 MB; the shard's `coverage-tools.txt` 14.4 MB after the dedupe — against unbounded growth before.
- `make -n coverage-shard SHARD=tools` shows `-coverprofile=…/build/gocoverdir/tools.txt` and `tail -n +2 …/build/gocoverdir/tools.txt >> coverage-tools.txt`; `python3 scripts/changelog.py check` passes.
- CI proof is this PR's `Go race coverage` job (the PR workflow merges the nine shard profiles) and develop's first pipeline after the merge.

## Checklist

- [x] `make test` and `make lint` pass locally (Makefile path change plus a hygiene test; the suite is otherwise unchanged)
- [x] Tests added or updated for the change
- [x] Documentation extended where it already covers the surface (see CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Changelog entry added as `changes/unreleased/<slug>.<section>.md`, not as an edit to `CHANGELOG.md`
- [x] baselines regenerated and `make docs-counts` run if a gate count moved (none moved)
- [x] No internal work-item labels (waves, slices, `F4`, `K5`) in the body, docs, or changelog

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+package hygiene
+
+import (
+	"path"
+	"regexp"
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+var (
+	makefileCoverageRecipe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?ms)^coverage:.*?\n\n`)
+	recipeProfileWrites    = regexp.MustCompile(`-coverprofile=(\S+)|-o (\S+)|tail -n \+2 (\S+) >>`)
+)
+
+// TestCoverageIntermediatesCannotBeAShardProfile: make coverage-shard collects into
+// coverage-<shard>.txt, so the recipe's intermediates live under GO_COUNTER_DIR and bear no shard's name.
+func TestCoverageIntermediatesCannotBeAShardProfile(t *testing.T) {
+	makefile := readRepoFile(t, "Makefile")
+	recipe := makefileCoverageRecipe.FindString(makefile)
+	if recipe == "" {
+		t.Fatal("Makefile: no coverage recipe")
+	}
+	config := readRepoFile(t, ".circleci/config.yml")
+	arrays := circleShardArrays.FindAllStringSubmatch(config, -1)
+	if len(arrays) != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("found %d shard arrays in .circleci/config.yml, want 2", len(arrays))
+	}
+	var forbidden []string
+	for _, shard := range append(strings.Fields(arrays[1][1]), strings.Fields(firstSubmatch(t, makefileCoverage, makefile, "Makefile COVERAGE_SHARDS"))...) {
+		forbidden = append(forbidden, "coverage-"+shard+".txt")
+	}
+	var intermediates int
+	for _, m := range recipeProfileWrites.FindAllStringSubmatch(recipe, -1) {
+		file := m[1] + m[2] + m[3]
+		if file == "$(COVERAGE_PROFILE)" {
+			continue
+		}
+		intermediates++
+		if !strings.HasPrefix(file, "$(GO_COUNTER_DIR)/") {
+			t.Errorf("coverage recipe writes %s outside GO_COUNTER_DIR, where a shard's coverage-<shard>.txt can collide with it", file)
+		}
+		if base := path.Base(file); slices.Contains(forbidden, base) || base == "coverage.txt" {
+			t.Errorf("coverage recipe intermediate %s is named like a shard's profile", file)
+		}
+	}
+	if intermediates < 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("coverage recipe: found %d intermediate profiles, want the counter and tools profiles", intermediates)
+	}
+}

task: Fix flaky `StateFilter` discovery cap search test
description:
This PR fixes the flaky `searches beyond the discovery cap and keeps deleted selected names` test in `state-filter.test.tsx`. It failed on `main` in [UI v2 Checks run 40103970615](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/40103970615) (commit 213a369488c4983e8c4e7256b6eb4b62ac5540d4) with `Unable to find role="menuitem" and name "Baseline, NOT Met"`.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and fix</summary>

`useStateOptions` debounces the search query by 300ms before it sends the `/observed-states?query=Base` request. The test types "Base" and then calls `findByRole`, which waits 1000ms by default. The 300ms debounce, the MSW response, and the re-render all had to finish inside that 1000ms. Instrumented local runs showed that the time from the end of typing to the request was 300–510ms under load. On a busy CI runner, the full sequence can go above 1000ms.

The fix uses `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` in this test, with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers })`. The test then calls `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(300)` after it types. This advances the debounce on purpose, so the debounce does not use the `findByRole` wait time. `afterEach` restores real timers. This is the same pattern as `rich-date-range-selector.test.tsx`.

Verification:
- Before the fix, the test failed 1 of 3 times when run alone on its own.
- After the fix, it passed 24 of 24 runs (3 rounds of 8 parallel runs on 8 cores). The full file passes.
- `npm run lint` and `npm run check` pass.

</details>

task: feat(release): announce each release on Slack
description:
## What and why

Each stable `v*` release is now announced in the maintainers' Slack channel. A new `release` workflow job, `announce-release-slack` ("Announce the release on Slack"), runs `scripts/release-announce.py` after "Publish GitHub release". It reads the release title and URL from the GitHub API and posts them as `{"text": ...}` to the Slack incoming webhook in `OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL`, which comes from the CircleCI context named `Slack`. A Slack app's incoming webhook cannot override channel, username or icon, so the payload carries only text. The post goes to the channel chosen when the webhook was added, under the app's own display name and icon. `--snippet FILE` appends hand-written text, such as install lines.

- The release title has `&`, `<` and `>` escaped as Slack's formatting rules require, so a title containing `<!channel>` or `<@U…>` cannot mention anyone. The snippet is passed through unescaped, because it is maintainer-written mrkdwn and may contain `<url|label>` links.
- A pre-release tag (`v1.2.3-rc.1`) is not announced: the script prints that it is skipping it and exits 0, before any GitHub or webhook call. This matches the other pre-release paths (TestPyPI, npm `next`, no MCP Registry publish).
- Not the GitHub Slack app's `releases` subscription, because it would also announce the two prereleases `nightly.yml` publishes every night (`nightly-<yyyymmdd>-<commit>` and `nightly`).
- The job does not depend on the registry publishers, and nothing depends on it. A missing context or webhook fails only this job.
- In a rehearsal the job prints the payload instead of posting it, for the tag `scripts/rehearsal-version.sh` derives (the version the branch will release). It also says whether `OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL` is set.

**Maintainer setup:** create a Slack app, enable Incoming Webhooks and use *Add New Webhook to Workspace* for the channel. That grants only the `incoming-webhook` scope; no bot token or `chat:write` is needed. Set the app's display name and icon in its settings. Then add the URL as `OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL` in a restricted CircleCI context named `Slack`. Whoever triggers a rehearsal now needs access to six contexts instead of five (`docs/project/releasing.md` is updated to say so).

## How it was verified

- New tests in `scripts/release-announce-test.py` (7 tests) cover:
  - building the payload: the title falls back to the tag, the snippet is appended, and the payload is exactly `{"text": ...}`
  - escaping: `<!channel>`, `<@U123>` and `&` in the title are escaped, and a `<url|label>` link in the snippet is kept as written
  - a pre-release tag is skipped with no network access and no webhook
  - `--dry-run`, with no network access
  - a real POST to a local HTTP server, checking the JSON body and the `Content-Type`
  - a webhook reply other than `ok` is refused
  - a missing `OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL` is reported by name, pointing at the `Slack` context
- The tests run beside the release provenance writer test in both CircleCI and the GitHub Actions pull-request checks (`.github/workflows/pr.yml`), and under `make scripts-coverage`.
- `circleci config validate`, `scripts/changelog.py check`, `check-doc-links.py`, `check-doc-ids.py` and `go test ./tests/hygiene` all pass.
- I ran a dry run against the v0.11.0 title by hand.
- Not exercised: a post from CircleCI to the real Slack webhook. That first happens on the next `v*` tag.

## Checklist

- [x] `make test` and `make lint` pass locally — no Go code changed; ran the gates listed above
- [x] Tests added or updated for the change
- [x] Documentation extended where it already covers the surface (see CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Changelog entry added as `changes/unreleased/<slug>.<section>.md`, not as an edit to `CHANGELOG.md`
- [x] baselines regenerated and `make docs-counts` run if a gate count moved (compliance rows need nothing: the census is counted at docs build) — no gate count moved
- [x] No internal work-item labels (waves, slices, `F4`, `K5`)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Post the Slack announcement of a released tag.
+
+Usage: scripts/release-announce.py --tag v1.2.3 [--snippet FILE] [--dry-run]
+
+The release workflow's announce-release-slack job runs this after the GitHub
+release exists. It reads the release's title and URL from the GitHub API (the
+release body stays human-written and can be edited up to the moment of the
+post), wraps them in a short Slack message and POSTs it to the incoming webhook
+in OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL. The optional --snippet file carries extra body text
+("Get it: pip install opensysml …"), appended verbatim so the announcement a
+release deserves can be hand-written without touching this script.
+The webhook posts to the channel chosen when it was added, under the Slack
+app's own name and icon.
+
+Environment:
+    OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL   incoming-webhook URL for the announcement channel
+    GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN/CIRCLE_TOKEN   token for the release API read
+    GH_REPO             owner/name, default from CIRCLE_PROJECT_USERNAME and
+                        CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME, else Open-MBEE/OpenSysML
+
+--dry-run prints the payload instead of posting; the release pipeline's
+rehearsal uses it so a rehearsal exercises everything but the POST.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import urllib.request
+from typing import Any
+
+
+def _env(*names: str) -> str:
+    for name in names:
+        value = os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
+        if value:
+            return value
+    return ""
+
+
+def _slack_escape(text: str) -> str:
+    return text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")
+
+
+def _github_release(repo: str, tag: str, token: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases/tags/{tag}"
+    request = urllib.request.Request(url)
+    request.add_header("Accept", "application/vnd.github+json")
+    if token:
+        request.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
+    try:
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:
+            return json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
+    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - report the HTTP status, not a stack
+        sys.exit(f"Error: reading release {tag} of {repo} failed: {error}")
+
+
+def build_payload(release_name: str, release_url: str, tag: str,
+                  snippet: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The Slack message for one release."""
+    title = _slack_escape(release_name.strip() or tag)
+    lines = [
+        f":tada: *{title}* is out!",
+        f"Release notes and downloads: {release_url}",
+    ]
+    if snippet.strip():
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append(snippet.rstrip())
+    return {"text": "\n".join(lines)}
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
+                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    parser.add_argument("--tag", required=True, help="release tag, e.g. v1.2.3")
+    parser.add_argument("--snippet", help="file with extra body lines to append verbatim")
+    parser.add_argument("--release-name", help="use this title instead of a GitHub API read")
+    parser.add_argument("--release-url", help="use this URL instead of a GitHub API read")
+    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
+                        help="print the payload instead of posting it")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    if "-" in args.tag:
+        print(f"Not announcing pre-release {args.tag}; only stable releases are announced.")
+        return 0
+
+    repo = _env("GH_REPO")
+    if not repo:
+        owner, name = _env("CIRCLE_PROJECT_USERNAME"), _env("CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME")
+        repo = f"{owner}/{name}" if owner and name else "Open-MBEE/OpenSysML"
+
+    snippet = ""
+    if args.snippet:
+        with open(args.snippet, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            snippet = handle.read()
+
+    if args.release_name or args.release_url:
+        release_name = args.release_name or args.tag
+        release_url = args.release_url or f"https://github.com/{repo}/releases/tag/{args.tag}"
+    else:
+        token = _env("GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "CIRCLE_TOKEN")
+        release = _github_release(repo, args.tag, token)
+        release_name = release.get("name") or args.tag
+        release_url = release.get("html_url") or f"https://github.com/{repo}/releases/tag/{args.tag}"
+
+    payload = build_payload(
+        release_name=release_name,
+        release_url=release_url,
+        tag=args.tag,
+        snippet=snippet,
+    )
+
+    if args.dry_run:
+        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
+        return 0
+
+    webhook = _env("OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL")
+    if not webhook:
+        sys.exit("Error: OPENSYSML_WEBHOOK_URL is not set; add the incoming-webhook "
+                 "URL to the 'Slack' context (Organization Settings -> Contexts).")
+    request = urllib.request.Request(
+        webhook,
+        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
+        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
+        method="POST",
+    )
+    try:
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:
+            body = response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+            if body.strip() != "ok":
+                sys.exit(f"Error: the Slack webhook answered {response.status} {body!r}")
+    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - report the HTTP status, not a stack
+        sys.exit(f"Error: posting to the Slack webhook failed: {error}")
+    print(f"Announced {args.tag} of {repo} to Slack.")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

task: fix(libs): key library records by document name as well as content
description:
## What and why

The library record cache (`internal/workspace/libs`, the `.idx` files under `sysml-ls/libs`) keyed a document's record on its content hash, the digest of the library set, the build ID and the format version, but not on the document's name. A library path holding two copies of the standard library therefore produced one key per file for both copies, and whichever copy was recorded last wrote the record both restored on the next start.

A record names the documents its facts refer to (`ElementRef.Doc`), and a parse of either copy resolves its same-file references within itself: `Parts::Part :> Items::Item` in copy A resolves to copy A's `Item`. Restored from copy B's record, copy A's `Part` pointed at copy B's `Item`, and so on through the hierarchy (2,925 of 21,786 library symbols had different direct supertypes on the warm load than on the cold one). A connection end, which reaches `Parts::Part` through both the end's own typing and the connection's, then inherited `self` through two chains that no longer met, and the inherited-name rule reported `Duplicate of inherited member name 'self' from Object, Part` on a warm start where a cold start reported nothing.

`Cache.keyFor`/`keyForSum` now take the document name, so two files of equal content in one set are two records, as the interface-record key already treats user documents (`docs/internals/interface-records.md`, "Cache key"). The loader passes each file's name. Old records are under keys no load produces any more and are pruned by age like any other stale record.

Also checked: the cache invalidates when `OPENSYSML_LIBRARY_PATH` changes between runs. The key's set digest covers the name and content of every file of the library, so switching between a one-copy and a two-copy tree over one cache directory misses on the first load of each tree (0 hits) and hits only on a tree already recorded under the same digest (110 and 220 hits respectively). No sibling bug there.

## Specification basis

Behaviour changes (before → after):

- Before → after: with two copies of a library file on the library path, a second start (index cache present) reported `Duplicate of inherited member name 'self' from Object, Part` on a connection end (and `'self' from Action, Part` on an action typed by a part definition) that the first start did not report. After: both starts report what the first did. The rule itself is unchanged: an owned or inherited member name a type also inherits from elsewhere is indistinguishable (KerML 8.3.2.4.5 / 8.4.3.2) only when the two chains reach two different members, and the two copies' `self` is one member reached twice once each copy restores its own facts.
- With one copy of the library nothing changes: every existing `Duplicate of inherited member name` test passes unchanged cold and warm.

What remains, outside this change: with two copies on the library path the parsed (cold) path itself differs from a one-copy library in a few of the inherited-name tests (a duplicated `'portions' from Occurrence`, `'start' from StateAction` on `state :>> start;`, `'payload' from MessageAction`) and in the argument-binding tests; those differ identically cold and warm after this change, so they are two-copy resolution behaviour of the parsed path rather than a cache divergence.

### Measured fallout

No golden, fixture, corpus expectation or baseline moved. Cache keys of every library record change (every record is rebuilt on the first start after upgrading, as after any format bump).

## How it was verified

### Tests

- `TestLoaderRestoresEachCopyFromItsOwnRecord` (`internal/workspace/libs/loader_copies_test.go`): two copies of a one-file library; the warm load restores every document from a record and gives every symbol the direct supertypes the cold load derived, each copy's `D :> B` within its own copy. task: docs(release): record the sequence-shaped results of 0.11.0 and tidy the fixtures the differential surfaced
description:
## What and why

A binary differential of v0.10.1 against v0.11.0 surfaced three loose ends; this PR settles them without changing any rule.

**Sequence-shaped results of 0.11.0 (docs).** Since 0.11.0 the CLI, the REPL and the clients report a calculation's result and a performed action's parameters in their multiplicity shape: `sysml -calc "P::Twice(3.0)"` prints `= [6.0]` where 0.10.1 printed `= 6.0`, `-action` prints an `out` parameter as `sum = [5]`, `-e "P::twice(2.0)"` prints `[4.0]`; a plain attribute read (`-e "P::p.w"`) still prints the scalar `4.0`. Reproduced with both tag builds on a small model. The 0.11.0 changelog does record this (the *Changed* entry "A calculation result with no stated multiplicity is held by its effective multiplicity, as an action's parameters are", the two *Fixed* entries on calc-result and performed-action pin shapes, and the recursive typed action body fix) — it is only absent from `develop`'s `CHANGELOG.md` until the 0.11.0 back-merge lands — so no second fragment is added. The only reader-facing example that still showed the pre-0.11.0 scalar is the `-calc` transcript in `docs/guide/03-command-line.md`; it now shows `= [80.0]` with one paragraph on why. The `-action` transcripts in `docs/guide/06-behavior.md` (`result = 84`, `taken = 1`) print attributes assigned in the body, which 0.11.0 still prints as scalars, and no client README prints a calc result, so those are unchanged.

The recursive typed action body crash is also already recorded: `internal/exec/runtime/testdata/conformance/action_recursive_typed_body.sysml` stack-overflows `sysml -validate` on v0.10.1 (`fatal error: stack overflow`, exit 2) and validates clean on v0.11.0; the fixing commit is ac2166348 (`feat(runtime): lower a typed action body nested in its own type when its performance starts`), which is in the 0.11.0 changelog.

**Spec example `sysml/8.4.17.1/3.sysml` adjudicated as a constraint erratum.** The example is `requirement def R3 specializes Requirements::RequirementCheck { actor a subsets ...actors; stakeholder s subsets ...stakeholders; }`. SysML 8.3.21.8 `validateRequirementDefinitionSubjectParameterPosition` reads: "The subjectParameter of a RequirementDefinition must be its first input. `input->notEmpty() and input->first() = subjectParameter`". `R3` declares no subject, so its `subjectParameter` is the inherited `RequirementCheck::subj`, while KerML 8.3.3.1.10 `deriveTypeFeatureMembership` orders the owned memberships before the inherited ones, so `input->first()` is the owned actor `a`: the constraint fires on the document's own example. The pinned pilot (0.62.0, `checkSubjectParameter` over `TypeUtil.getInputOf`) agrees: `3.sysml:4:5: error: Subject must be first parameter.` Ours reports the same, so the pass, the ratchet (`1 sysml/8.4.17.1/3.sysml`) and the pilot baselines are unchanged; the file now has its row in `docs/project/spec-examples.md` under a new "constraints of the same document reject" erratum table, and the erratum count moves 29 → 30.

**Fixture hygiene (eight rewrites, no rule changes).** The execution and view harnesses gate only parse diagnostics, so these models carried constraint errors that `sysml -validate` reports and the pinned pilot reports identically. Every one was the model's fault:

| Fixture | Diagnostic | Rewrite |
|---|---|---|
| `filter_classification_annotation_forms.sysml` | `feature-reference-referent` on `Belt @ Safety` (operand of `@` names a definition) | `#Safety part belt;` and `belt @ Safety`; the `#`-prefix annotation form is still exercised |
| `filter_classification_meta_versus_annotation.sysml` | same | `#Safety part belt : Belt;` and `belt @ Safety`; `Belt @@ Safety` stays, since `@@` takes any element |
| `value_classification_at.sysml` | same, last operand | `Belt @@ Safety` (the metadata test on a definition the comment describes) |
| `view_exposed_element_classification.sysml` | same, twice | `Lib::Belt @@ Safety and not (Lib::Radio @@ Safety)` |
| `

task: feat(npm): publish the MCP runner also as @openmbee/opensysml-mcp
description:
## What and why

The MCP server's npm runner is published as `@openmbee/sysml-mcp` plus five `@openmbee/sysml-mcp-<os>-<cpu>` platform packages. The other OpenSysML npm packages are named `@openmbee/opensysml*`, so the server is now **also** installable as `npx -y @openmbee/opensysml-mcp`. Nothing is renamed or deprecated; the platform package names are untouched.

`@openmbee/opensysml-mcp` has no source tree of its own. `client/node/scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs` generates it from `packaging/npm/sysml-mcp` (into `client/node/packages/opensysml-mcp`) whenever it builds the `sysml-mcp` platform packages: the same `bin/`, `lib/` and README, the manifest renamed, `opensysml-mcp` as a second command beside `sysml-mcp` (npx runs the one named for the package), the same five platform packages pinned at the version being built, and no `mcpName` — the MCP Registry listing (`packaging/mcp/server.json`) stays on `@openmbee/sysml-mcp` alone. This matches the shape of `@openmbee/opensysml-mcp@0.11.0`, which the maintainer published by hand from the `v0.11.0` tree; `docs/project/releasing.md` records that and that the job's "already published" refusal sees it as published like any other version.

Wiring:
- `.circleci/config.yml` `publish-npm`: the refusal step counts fourteen names (alias included), a new step packs the generated alias into `dist/npm` and checks version / pins / both commands / no `mcpName` before `npm whoami`, and the alias is published last, after `@openmbee/sysml-mcp`; the rehearsal path packs with `--dry-run` as before and skips `npm publish` by name.
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`: packs and publishes fourteen tarballs, alias last; checks the alias manifest; the `latest` dist-tag check covers the alias.
- `scripts/npm-mcp-test.sh` (run by the PR workflow, `publish-npm` and the nightly): also installs the packed alias beside this platform's package and runs `opensysml-mcp -version`, `sysml-mcp -version` and the stdio probe through `opensysml-mcp`.
- `tests/hygiene`: `release_config_test.go` and `nightly_workflow_test.go` pin the counts and the publish order; new `mcp_alias_test.go` pins the generator, that no committed `package.json` names the alias, the proof script, the registry staying on `@openmbee/sysml-mcp`, and that every page naming `npx -y @openmbee/sysml-mcp` names the alias too.
- Docs: `docs/project/releasing.md` (fourteen packages, the alias paragraph, the hand-published 0.11.0, nightly trusted-publisher note), `README.md`, `docs/guide/01-install.md`, `docs/guide/08-editors.md`, `docs/reference/sysml-mcp.md`, `packaging/npm/sysml-mcp/README.md`; changelog fragment `changes/unreleased/npm-opensysml-mcp-alias.added.md`.

Lockstep: the alias carries the runner's version, so the lockstep bump (`packaging/npm/sysml-mcp/package.json`, `check_version.py`, `snapshot_version.py --stamp`) needs no new file.

## How it was verified

- `npx -y ./openmbee-opensysml-mcp-0.11.0.tgz -version` with the alias generated at 0.11.0 from this tree and the platform package resolved from registry.npmjs.org: installs `@openmbee/sysml-mcp-linux-x64@0.11.0`, prints `sysml-mcp v0.11.0`; npx's cache shows `.bin/opensysml-mcp` and `.bin/sysml-mcp`.
- Local tarballs (alias + platform; alias + `@openmbee/sysml-mcp` + platform): both `npx opensysml-mcp -version` and `npx sysml-mcp -version` run the platform binary; installing both runners together links both bin names to the same shim without error.

 - **Language Server** — A standard LSP server (`sysml-lsp`) with live diagnostics, semantic hover, go-to-definition, find references, completion, signature help, workspace-wide symbol search, formatting, rename, semantic tokens, quick fixes, code lenses and inlay hints. A VS Code extension with TextMate grammars for `.sysml` and `.kerml` ships in [editors/vscode](editors/vscode) — its diagram panel draws the model beside the editor with zoom, pan and fit, click-to-select highlighting, show/hide of relationship kinds, drag-to-layout and an ELK auto layout that writes nothing — and any editor with a generic LSP client can drive the server directly — [guide chapter 8](docs/guide/08-editors.md) walks through both. *Not yet:* the extension is not on a marketplace — install the nightly `opensysml-sysml.vsix` or build it from source — and the server answers no semantic token delta requests.
 - **Interactive REPL** — An exploratory modeling environment: define models incrementally, evaluate expressions interactively, instantiate parts, run calculations and inspect runtime state, comparable to IPython or Jupyter for systems engineering.
 - **Jupyter Kernel** — `sysml-jupyter-kernel` runs the REPL session behind the Jupyter protocol, so notebook cells hold SysML: declarations accumulate across cells, expressions evaluate, every `%` command works as at the prompt, and views and documents render as Mermaid, SVG, Markdown, tables, HTML or JSON. `pip install jupyter-opensysml-kernel && python -m jupyter_opensysml_kernel install` registers it ([guide chapter 12](docs/guide/12-jupyter.md)).
-- **MCP Server for Coding Agents** — `sysml-mcp` serves the toolchain to OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code Copilot, Gemini CLI, Devin and any other Model Context Protocol host over stdio: the language server's workspace, the runtime's one-shot service and persistent REPL sessions as tools an agent calls. `npx -y @openmbee/sysml-mcp` runs it with nothing preinstalled, `sysml-mcp -http 8765` serves one long-lived server over Streamable HTTP for remote agents or several agents over one workspace (loopback as it is, any other address behind a bearer token), and `sysml-mcp -print-config <host>` writes the host's configuration block, in URL form with `-http` ([MCP server reference](docs/reference/sysml-mcp.md)).

 - **Constraint Solving** *(experimental)* — In addition to evaluating what holds of an object, an external SMT solver determines whether a constraint, requirement or satisfaction assertion *can* hold, which conditions conflict when it cannot, which values would satisfy it, which variants a model permits, and what optimizes an `analysis def`'s objectives. The solver is optional and discovered at runtime. [The REPL command reference](docs/reference/repl-commands.md) documents each command, and [installing a solver](docs/guide/01-install.md#installing-a-solver-optional) describes how to obtain one. The design follows OpenMBEE's [HMF](https://github.com/hivecore-dev/hmf) (see [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements)).
 - **Embeddable Go API** — `client/opensysml` is the public Go surface: parse, look up symbols, evaluate expressions and instantiate parts from Go code, answered in process by the engine the calling binary already links (no port, no child process and no serialization round trip), or over the Connect protocol against an externally hosted service. See [client/opensysml/README.md](client/opensysml/README.md).
 - **Python Client Library** — gRPC-based Python bindings for programmatic access: parse models, resolve symbols, evaluate expressions, instantiate parts, execute actions/state machines. Includes IPython display hooks for Jupyter notebooks and pandas DataFrame integration. Constraint, requirement, satisfaction and calc verdicts are available as RPCs (`verify_constraint`, `verify_requirement`, `verify_satisfaction`, `calc`).

--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/hygiene/mcp_alias_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+package hygiene
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"io/fs"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// mcpAliasPackage is the runner's second npm name, matching the other
+// OpenSysML packages; the generator derives it from packaging/npm/sysml-mcp.
+const mcpAliasPackage = "@openmbee/opensysml-mcp"
+
+// TestNpmRunnerAliasIsGeneratedFromTheRunner pins how @openmbee/opensysml-mcp
+// exists: not as a second source tree but generated by the platform-package
+// generator from packaging/npm/sysml-mcp, with `opensysml-mcp` beside
+// `sysml-mcp`, the runner's platform packages pinned at the built version and
+// no registry name; proved by the npm runner test through both commands; named
+// beside the runner wherever a user is told the npm name; and recorded in the
+// release procedure with the hand-published 0.11.0.
+func TestNpmRunnerAliasIsGeneratedFromTheRunner(t *testing.T) {
+	const generator = "client/node/scripts/build-platform-packages.mjs"
+	requireFragments(t, generator, readRepoFile(t, generator),
+		`const MCP_ALIAS = "`+mcpAliasPackage+`";`,
+		`function buildMCPAlias(args) {`,
+		`join(args.out, "opensysml-mcp")`,
+		`cpSync(join(mcpRoot, part), join(directory, part), { recursive: true });`,
+		`delete manifest.mcpName;`,
+		`manifest.bin = { "sysml-mcp": shim, "opensysml-mcp": shim };`,
+		`manifest.optionalDependencies = Object.fromEntries(platforms.map((name) => [name, args.version]));`,
+		`built.push(buildMCPAlias(args));`,
+	)
+
+	// One source tree: no committed package.json names the alias.
+	err := filepath.WalkDir("../..", func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if d.IsDir() {
+			switch d.Name() {
+			case ".git", "node_modules", "build", "bin", "site", "packages":
+				return fs.SkipDir
+			}
+			return nil
+		}
+		if d.Name() != "package.json" {
+			return nil
+		}
+		raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		var pkg struct {
+			Name string `json:"name"`
+		}
+		if json.Unmarshal(raw, &pkg) == nil && pkg.Name == mcpAliasPackage {
+			t.Errorf("%s names %s; the alias is generated from packaging/npm/sysml-mcp, never kept as a copy", path, mcpAliasPackage)
+		}
+		return nil
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("walk the tree: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	const proof = "scripts/npm-mcp-test.sh"
+	requireFragments(t, proof, readRepoFile(t, proof),
+		`alias_dir="$packages/opensysml-mcp"`,
+		`[[ "$alias_name" == "`+mcpAliasPackage+`" ]]`,
+		`"$tarballs/openmbee-opensysml-mcp-$version.tgz"`,
+		`for command in opensysml-mcp sysml-mcp; do`,
+		`"$alias_project/node_modules/.bin/opensysml-mcp" -root "$workspace"`,
+	)
+
+	// The registry listing stays with the runner.
+	server, raw := loadMCPRegistryServer(t)
+	if len(server.Packages) != 1 || server.Packages[0].Identifier != mcpRegistryPackage || strings.Contains(raw, mcpAliasPackage) {
+		t.Errorf("%s lists %d packages (%q); the registry entry is %s alone, the alias declares no mcpName", mcpRegistryServerJSON, len(server.Packages), raw, mcpRegistryPackage)

task: ci(release): let the Maven Central publish step outlive the plugin's wait for the published state
description:
## What and why

The v0.11.0 release pipeline's `Publish opensysml to Maven Central` job went red for a version that is on Central. Its `Sign, upload and publish` step log shows the upload succeeded and the wait began:

```
Uploaded bundle successfully, deployment name: Deployment, deploymentId: 058959b8-cc49-459d-992d-c349d399ca84. Deployment will publish automatically
Waiting until Deployment 058959b8-cc49-459d-992d-c349d399ca84 is published
Too long with no output (exceeded 10m0s): context deadline exceeded
```

`central-publishing-maven-plugin` 0.12.0 with `waitUntil=published` polls Central every `waitPollingInterval` seconds for up to `waitMaxTime` seconds (both default to their floors of 5 s and 1800 s; the plugin raises lower values) and logs the per-poll status at debug level only, so at Maven's default log level the step is silent for the whole wait. CircleCI's default `no_output_timeout` of 10 minutes therefore killed the step while Central was still publishing; the version landed shortly after, and the `Refuse a version already on Central` step correctly forbids re-running the job.

Changes:

- `.circleci/config.yml`: the publish step gets `no_output_timeout: 35m`, above the plugin's `waitMaxTime + waitPollingInterval` bound of 30 min 5 s, so a slow publish is decided by the plugin (which fails the build with `DeploymentPublishTimedOutException` after 30 minutes) rather than by CircleCI mid-wait. The `release_rehearsal` path is untouched.
- `client/java/pom.xml`: `waitMaxTime=1800` and `waitPollingInterval=5` are set explicitly so the pom states the bound the CircleCI timeout is sized against. `autoPublish=true` and `waitUntil=published` are unchanged.
- `tests/hygiene/release_config_test.go`: `TestMavenPublishStepOutlivesThePluginWait` reads both files and fails if the step loses its `no_output_timeout`, if the timeout no longer exceeds `waitMaxTime + waitPollingInterval`, if either value is set below the plugin's floor (which would misdescribe the wait), or if `autoPublish`/`waitUntil` are weakened.
- `docs/project/releasing.md`: the Maven Central job description names the two timeouts and their relation, and the failure section says what a red Maven Central job means now (a plugin timeout after 30 minutes with the version possibly still landing on Central; check Central before considering a re-run, and a version already there is refused by design).
- `changes/unreleased/maven-central-publish-wait.fixed.md`.

## How it was verified

- `circleci config validate .circleci/config.yml` → `Config file at ".circleci/config.yml" is valid.`
- `mvn -B -q -f client/java/pom.xml -Prelease -Dgpg.skip validate` → exit 0 (the plugin accepts the two parameters).
- `go test -count=1 ./tests/hygiene/...` → ok; `go vet ./tests/hygiene/`, `gofmt -l tests/hygiene` clean.
- Mutation checks of the new test: `no_output_timeout: 30m` fails (does not outlive 30m5s), removing the timeout fails, `waitMaxTime=600` fails (below the plugin floor).
- `python3 scripts/changelog.py check`, `python3 scripts/check-doc-links.py`, `python3 scripts/check-doc-ids.py`, `python3 scripts/check-doc-figures.py` all pass.
- Plugin behaviour read from the 0.12.0 source (`PublishMojo` floors, `DeploymentPublishedWatcherImpl` debug-level polling and timeout exception) and the plugin's documentation.

## Checklist

- [x] `make test` and `make lint` pass locally (touched areas: hygiene suite, config validation, changelog and docs checks)
- [x] Tests added or updated for the change
- [x] Documentation extended where it already covers the surface (see CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Changelog entry added as `changes/unreleased/<slug>.<section>.md`, not as an edit to `CHANGELOG.md`
- [ ] baselines regenerated and `make docs-counts` run if a gate count moved (no gate count moved)
- [x] No internal work-item labels (waves, slices, `F4`, `K5`) in the body, docs, or changelog

task: fix(router): route decisions calls only to deployments whose provider supports decisions
description:
When one model group mixes an OpenAI deployment with a Bedrock deployment, `/v1/decisions` calls could land on the Bedrock one and always fail with a 400, since Bedrock has no Decisions support. The router now skips deployments whose provider has no Decisions support, and keeps every deployment when none of them can serve it so the provider error still comes back

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Decisions calls on a mixed group hit the Bedrock deployment and 400
- That 400 is never retried on the OpenAI deployment in the same group
- Latency routing after chat traffic sends every Decisions call to Bedrock

How it solves it:

- Decisions calls only route to deployments whose provider has a Decisions config
- Uses the same provider config lookup that Decisions dispatch already uses
- If no deployment qualifies, the full list is kept and the provider error comes back
- Chat and every other call type route exactly as before

## User Flow

Before: a developer sends Decisions calls to a model group that has an OpenAI and a Bedrock deployment, and some or all of them fail

1. The proxy admin puts an OpenAI deployment and a Bedrock deployment under one `model_name`
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/decisions with that `model_name`
3. Some calls come back 400 `Unknown Decisions provider 'bedrock'`, and with latency routing after chat traffic all of them do

After: the same Decisions calls all succeed on the OpenAI deployment

1. The proxy admin puts an OpenAI deployment and a Bedrock deployment under one `model_name`
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/decisions with that `model_name`
3. Every call comes back 200 with `x-litellm-model-id` naming the OpenAI deployment, while chat calls still use both deployments

task: feat(assistant): answer Keiki preflight checks so bad calls never reach the Face ID card
description:
## Description

Zero's write tools now opt in to Keiki's new `policy.preflight` ([Mail-0/sms-kit#1780](https://github.com/Mail-0/sms-kit/pull/1780)).

Before Keiki shows the Face ID approval card, it sends the call once with `context.preflight: true`. The `/tools/:tool` hook runs all of its usual checks, then returns `{ ok: true, preflight: true }` without recording or running anything. The checks are: owner auth, `ownedMailbox`, tool argument parsing, the `mail:request_action` scope, `traceId`, and the `senderConnectionId` mailbox. If any check fails, the hook returns its error status, and Keiki sends that error back to the model instead of asking the owner.

This fixes what happened in the live test. The model sent `send_email` with `connectionId: "gmail"`, the owner approved it with Face ID, and only then was it rejected with `mailbox_selection_required`. With preflight, the model gets that error before any card is shown, so it can call `list_mailboxes` and try again.

Deploy order: merge this after sms-kit#1780 is live, then rerun `assistant:setup` so the gateway's tool policies include `preflight: true`. Until #1780 is deployed, Keiki rejects `preflight` as an unknown policy field, so the setup run would fail.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Areas Affected

- [x] API Endpoints

## Testing Done

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: a new `assistant.test.ts` case covers a valid preflight returning `{ ok: true, preflight: true }`, a `gmail` selector returning 400 `mailbox_selection_required`, nothing executed and no action row. The tool-policy expectation now includes `preflight: true`. `vitest run src/lib/assistant.test.ts` passes (57 tests). eslint is clean on the changed files.

## Security Considerations

- [x] Authentication checks are in place: preflight returns only after the same owner, scope and mailbox checks as a real call, and never executes or records anything.

task: fix(engine): trust newer Mozilla root CAs in the sandbox
description:
## Checklist

- [x] Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/TracecatHQ/tracecat/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] PR title is short and non-generic.
- [x] PR only implements a single feature or fixes a single bug.
- [x] Lint / pre-commits passing.

## Description

`run_python` and agent sandboxes verify TLS with OpenSSL's defaults: `/usr/lib/ssl/cert.pem`, which links to `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` in the sandbox rootfs. That file is Debian bookworm's `ca-certificates`, not the app's certifi, and it lags Mozilla. Compared with certifi 2026.10.19, the current image is missing 10 roots: TrustAsia TLS RSA/ECC, SECOM TLS 2024 RSA/ECC, SwissSign RSA TLS 2022-1, OISTE Server G1 RSA/ECC, Telia TLS v3 RSA/EC, and e-Szigno TLS 2023. Endpoints that chain to these roots fail verification in the sandbox even though they work everywhere else.

`docker/add_certifi_roots.py` runs in the `sandbox-rootfs` stage:

```
certifi wheel (URL + sha256 from uv.lock, hash-verified)
  -> roots not already in the Debian bundle (DER comparison)
  -> /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/certifi/*.crt
  -> update-ca-certificates
```

The `base` stage copies the same `.crt` files and runs `update-ca-certificates`, so host-side processes get the same roots. That includes the `direct` executor backend and `git`/`curl`.

Bumping `certifi` in `uv.lock` now also updates the sandbox trust store.

## Regression safety

- Roots are only added. The script never replaces the bundle with certifi, because Debian still ships 36 roots that Mozilla has removed (e.g. DigiCert Global Root CA, GlobalSign Root CA R1, Baltimore, Entrust). Dropping them could break legacy chains that work today.
- The certifi wheel is fetched from the locked URL and rejected if its hash doesn't match `uv.lock`. It is unpacked only to read `cacert.pem` and is not installed in the sandbox.
- The `sandbox-rootfs` and `base` targets build locally. Both bundles go from 148 to 158 roots, Python's default context lists the new roots, and HTTPS to pypi.org and github.com still succeeds.

## Related Issues

Companion chart PR: https://github.com/TracecatHQ/k8s/pull/197 adds `executor.extraVolumes`/`extraVolumeMounts` (and the same for `agentExecutor`), so operators can mount their own bundle over the sandbox trust store without a new image.

## Steps to QA

1. `docker build --target sandbox-rootfs -t rootfs .`
2. `docker run --rm rootfs python -c "import ssl; print(len(ssl.create_default_context().get_ca_certs()))"` should print `158`. Before this change it printed `148`.

+# Sandboxed code verifies TLS against this OS bundle, not the app's certifi.
+COPY docker/add_certifi_roots.py /tmp/add_certifi_roots.py
+RUN --mount=type=bind,source=uv.lock,target=/tmp/uv.lock \
+    python /tmp/add_certifi_roots.py /tmp/uv.lock && rm /tmp/add_certifi_roots.py
+

 # rootfs read-only, so every sandboxed Python process would recompile the

     && apt-get -y upgrade \
     && apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
 
+# Same roots for host-side processes, e.g. the direct executor backend.
+COPY --from=sandbox-rootfs /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/certifi /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/certifi
+RUN update-ca-certificates
+
 # DuckDB (CLI binary + extensions) is stored as a single physical copy inside
 # the sandbox rootfs (copied in below). The executor host — including the
 # in-process DuckDB Python package used by core.duckdb.execute_sql — reaches it
diff --git a/docker/add_certifi_roots.py b/docker/add_certifi_roots.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..355c880436
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docker/add_certifi_roots.py
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+"""Add the locked certifi roots that Debian's ca-certificates bundle lacks.
+
+Debian stable's bundle lags Mozilla's root program, so code that relies on
+OpenSSL defaults rejects certificates chaining to newer public roots. Roots
+are only added, never removed, so chains to roots Debian still ships keep
+working.
+"""
+
+import base64
+import hashlib
+import io
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tomllib
+import urllib.request
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SYSTEM_BUNDLE = Path("/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt")
+TARGET_DIR = Path("/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/certifi")
+PEM_BLOCK = re.compile(
+    r"-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\s+(.+?)\s+-----END CERTIFICATE-----", re.DOTALL
+)
+
+
+def pem_blocks(text: str) -> list[tuple[bytes, str]]:
+    return [
+        (base64.b64decode("".join(m.group(1).split())), m.group(0))
+        for m in PEM_BLOCK.finditer(text)
+    ]
+
+
+def locked_certifi_bundle(lock_path: Path) -> str:
+    lock = tomllib.loads(lock_path.read_text())
+    package = next(p for p in lock["package"] if p["name"] == "certifi")
+    wheel = next(w for w in package["wheels"] if w["url"].endswith("-none-any.whl"))
+    algorithm, expected = wheel["hash"].split(":", 1)
+    with urllib.request.urlopen(wheel["url"], timeout=60) as response:
+        data = response.read()
+    if hashlib.new(algorithm, data).hexdigest() != expected:
+        raise SystemExit(f"certifi wheel hash mismatch: {wheel['url']}")
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive:
+        return archive.read("certifi/cacert.pem").decode()
+
+
+def main(lock_path: Path) -> None:
+    system = {der for der, _ in pem_blocks(SYSTEM_BUNDLE.read_text())}
+    missing = [
+        pem
+        for der, pem in pem_blocks(locked_certifi_bundle(lock_path))
+        if der not in system
+    ]
+    TARGET_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    for pem in missing:
+        digest = hashlib.sha256(pem.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
+        (TARGET_DIR / f"certifi-{digest}.crt").write_text(pem + "\n")
+    subprocess.run(["update-ca-certificates"], check=True)
+    print(f"Added {len(missing)} certifi roots to {SYSTEM_BUNDLE}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main(Path(sys.argv[1]))

task: fix: acquire microphone before creating the web call
description:
Related: PRISM-1083 (Zeals)

## Problem

About 40% of Zeals' web-widget calls end with `assistant-did-not-receive-customer-audio`.

`vapi.start()` sends `POST /call/web` before it creates the Daily call object, and the mic is only requested later, inside `join()`. As a result, a backend call is created and billed even when the user denies or ignores the mic prompt. The backend then times out after `customerJoinTimeoutSeconds` (15s by default).

## Fix

```
start():
  track = await microphoneAcquire()   // getUserMedia, before POST /call/web
  webCall = POST /call/web
  Daily.createCallObject({ audioSource: track, ... })   // reuse the track, no second acquisition
```

- **On failure** (denied, no device, empty stream, `mediaDevices` unavailable): no backend call is made. `start()` emits `call-start-failed` with `stage: 'microphone-preflight'` and `error` with `type: 'microphone-preflight-<DOMException name>'`, then returns `null`.
- **Device selection:** a device-ID `audioSource` becomes `{ deviceId: { exact } }`. A caller-supplied `MediaStreamTrack` is reused as-is and never stopped by the SDK.
- **Track cleanup:** the SDK stops its own track in `cleanup()`, in `stop()`, and on API or join failure.
- **Pending prompt:** `stop()` cancels it (`AbortError`), and a track granted late is stopped. A concurrent second `start()` returns `null`. There's no timeout; `stop()` is the way out.
- **Opt-out:** on by default. Disable it with `vapi.start(assistant, ..., { microphonePreflightEnabled: false })` (`StartCallOptions`).
- Cleanup of an existing call object now happens before preflight instead of after the API call.

## Verification

Tested in real Chrome with a fake mic device and native permission prompts, comparing published `@vapi-ai/web@3.0.0` against this branch. I checked each attempt via `GET /call`.

| Scenario | Backend call created? | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0.0, mic denied | Yes | `silence-timed-out` |
| 3.0.0, prompt ignored >20s | Yes | `assistant-did-not-receive-customer-audio` |
| This PR, mic denied | **No** | `microphone-preflight-NotAllowedError` |
| This PR, mic allowed | Yes | greeting played, `stop()` worked |
| This PR, prompt pending, then `stop()` | **No** | `microphone-preflight-AbortError`, no hang |

![before/after](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..Ftl4pqC77zGZztmcKPICj1Db1eD6iqP4OvV6rV0qlHY)

![test recording](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjpudWxsLCJidWNrZXRfbmFtZSI6ImRldmluYXR0YWNobWVudHMiLCJidWNrZXRfa2V5IjoiYXR0YWNobWVudHNfcHJpdmF0ZS9vcmdfeDgzMHFFaUNHMTlpNzZGNi8zNjdjY2JjNi00ODU5LTQ5NDItYThkZC1mYjJkNjU0MDA2NzQiLCJpYXQiOjE3OTI3MDg5MjAsIm9yZ19pZCI6Im9yZ194ODMwcUVpQ0cxOWk3NkY2IiwiZmlsZW5hbWUiOiJwcmV2aWV3LndlYnAifQ.OFTEDflAOdB39_EIuPDM-bNwP1fHR-iv4OXc26EEycY)

New `__tests__/microphone-preflight.test.ts`. `npm run build` passes and `npm test` passes 73/73.

Not tested: a physical mic, iOS Safari, iframe mic policy, and the opt-out path in a browser (the opt-out has a unit test).

The widgets (`client-sdk-html-script-tag`, `client-sdk-react`) pin SDK 2.x, so they need a version bump to pick this up.
